figures.title: What each trajectory mode does
figures.message: Each simulated mode changes group B's trajectory in one geometric way, read by one statistic: magnitude scales it (size δ), orientation rotates it (θ), shape bends it (shape), and translation moves it without changing any of the three.
caveats: Constructed coordinates, not data or a fitted space.
Magnitude scales by 1.6 and orientation rotates by 35° about stage 1; shape moves the interior stage only, so it needs at least three stages.

figures.title: The four modes as the generator realizes them
figures.message: The numpy generator realizes each mode on a shared baseline: group B's stage-mean path is scaled, rotated, bent or shifted against group A's, and coincides with it at zero effect.

sources.measurement: generator input (no measurement)

caveats: Display projection: per panel, the first two principal axes of the six group × stage means of the concatenated standardized blocks; translation's offset is orthogonal to the stage geometry, so its panel's second axis is the group offset. It is not the measurement space (the double-CV PLS latent space).

One dataset per mode from generate_showcase_datasets (seed given in the manifest, n = 1,000, 3 stages, e = 1.0, surgery_censoring='clamp' as in the showcase); the modes share group A's baseline draw but are not otherwise identical.
Axes are flipped so group A runs from stage 1 toward positive values (translation: B above A); the sign carries nothing.
Rendered with seed 0 and n = 1,000 per dataset.

figures.message: At n = 1,200 each mode is detected by its target statistic; magnitude moves size alone, while rotating or bending a trajectory also changes its size (and rotation its shape).

figures.message: At n = 80 (the SEA-AD scale) only magnitude stays specific: orientation moves all three statistics about equally and shape moves size more than shape, so one significant statistic does not name the mode.

figures.title: Power against sample size
figures.message: Power rises with n for every statistic and with the third block: size (δ) is well powered by n = 200 at e = 0.1, shape needs n ≈ 500 with two blocks, and orientation stays below 0.75 even at n = 500.

figures.title: A weak stage signal inflates the rank
figures.message: As the joint stage effect weakens from δ = 2 to 0.25, the CV-selected rank inflates (median 2 to 11) and size and shape lose their power while the stage stays almost perfectly classified; orientation peaks at intermediate δ.

figures.title: Net displacement measures orientation better
figures.message: On identical datasets, net displacement doubles orientation power at n = 80 (0.300 → 0.648 at e = 1) and lifts it at n = 1,200 (0.840 → 0.924), while removing the shape mode's leak into θ.
